en: The *Vasudhārādhāraṇīsūtra*, the Noble *Vasudhārādhāraṇīsūtra*: Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed Noble Lady Śrī Vasudhārā!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the great city of Kauśāmbī,

in the Ghoṣitārāma, within the excellent great forest known as Kaṇṭaka, together with a great community of monks consisting of about five hundred monks, and with a vast multitude of śrāvakas and incalculable bodhisattvas endowed with all the qualities of a Buddha.
There, indeed, the Blessed One, surrounded and honored by that very assembly, was teaching the Dharma discourse named *The Complete Drying Up of the Ocean of Suffering from All Poverty and Disease*.

He fully proclaimed the holy life (*brahmacarya*)— good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, excellent in meaning and excellent in phrasing, absolute, complete, pure, and radiant.
Now at that time, in the great city of Kauśāmbī, there lived a householder named Sucandra.
His faculties were tranquil and his mind was serene; he had many sons, many daughters, and was endowed with a large retinue of servants. He was faithful, a man of great faith.

Then, at that time, the householder named Sucandra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Sucandra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"I would like to ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to have my question answered.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra:
"Ask, householder, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind with the answering of those questions."
When this had been said, the householder Sucandra, having replied to the Blessed One, "Excellent, Blessed One," addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, how does a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having been poor, become no longer poor? And having been ill, how does he become no longer ill?"
Then the Blessed One, though already knowing, addressed the householder Sucandra:
"Householder, why do you ask this question concerning poverty?
When this was said, the householder Sucandra spoke thus to the Blessed One.

“I am poor, Blessed One; I am poor, Sugata. I have many dependents, many sons, many daughters, and am endowed with many servants and attendants. Therefore, may the Blessed One teach this Dharma-discourse by which impoverished beings may become no longer poor, and sick beings may become free from sickness.”
They shall be endowed with abundant wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses;
they shall be beloved, pleasing, most charming, and beautiful to behold; they shall be masters of generosity.
May they be great lords of generosity, possessing inexhaustible stores of gold, bullion, wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries;
may they be enriched with jewels, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, silver, emeralds, and rubies;
and may they have well-established homes, sons, wives, and households.
"And they would possess a retinue complete with householder wives, sons, daughters, female slaves, laborers, and servants.
When this had been said, the Blessed One, with a Brahma-voice that fulfills all hopes, addressed the householder Sucandra as follows:
"Householder, in the past, in a time long gone, incalculable eons ago, at that time..."

At that time, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Bhagavān Śrīvajradharasāgaranirghoṣa— one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
In the presence of that Tathāgata, O householder, I heard the dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā;
having heard it, I took it up, retained it, recited it, taught it, mastered it, rejoiced in it,
and revealed it extensively to others.
I too, noble son, shall now speak those dhāraṇīs to you in such a way that,
through the power of this dhāraṇī, noble son, humans do not cause harm and non-humans do not cause harm.
The gods do not cause harm;
the nāgas do not cause harm;
the yakṣas do not cause harm.
The asuras do not harass them;
the rākṣasas do not harass them;
the bhūtas do not harass them.
Pretas do not harass them;
piśācas do not harass them;
kumbhāṇḍas do not harass them.
The Ostāḍakas do not harass them; the Apasmāras do not harass them;
the Gandharvas do not harass them.
The kinnaras do not harass them;
the mahoragas do not harass them;
the pūtanas do not harass them.
The kaṭapūtanas do not harass them;
all seizing spirits do not harass them;
all gods do not harass them.

Hunger and thirst do not afflict them; no foods whatsoever afflict them— likewise, up to those whose food consists of flowers, fruits, leaves, bark, stalks, roots, perfumes, incense, lamps, garlands, or sacrificial oblations, none of these afflict them.

Those who feed on vital energy, those who feed on sweat, those who feed on lymph, those who feed on blood, those who feed on flesh, those who feed on fat, those who feed on bone, those who feed on marrow, those who feed on semen, and those who feed on life—none of them cause harm.

Likewise, even those who feed on excrement, urine, saliva, mucus, moisture, phlegm, vomit, or what is not vomited—even those who feed on vomit do not cause harm; those who feed on crops and those who feed on embryos—all of them do not cause harm.
All ḍākinīs do not cause harm;
shadows do not cause harm;
and birth-pangs do not cause harm.
Those who subsist on meditative cultivation do not cause harm.

Those who subsist on forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles; those who subsist on oblations; those who subsist on various forms, deformed forms, infinite forms, forms at will, diverse forms, strength, nourishment, impurity, manifold things, and even leftovers—these do not cause harm.

As long as those who move through the air, those who move on the earth, those who move in the intermediate space, those who move in the water, and those who move on land—none of them shall cause harm.

For all these sentient beings, with my great vajra, for the purpose of striking, splitting, and crushing their heads: HŪṂ 2 PHAṬ! With the vajra, slay 2, dry up 2, paralyze 2, bind 2, and kill 2 all the wicked ones and all enemies! HANA!
2 daha 2 paca 2 mara 2 māraya 2 sarvaśatrūn nāśaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.

And for whichever son of good family, O Householder, this *dhāraṇī* named Vasudhārā is present in the heart, present in the home, present in the hand, present in the book, or has merely been heard and mastered by a faithful son of good family or daughter of good family—

If it has been well-considered by the mind, retained, recited, written down, rejoiced in, and extensively proclaimed to others, that will become for that son of good family or daughter of good family a source of long-term purpose, benefit, happiness, security, abundance, and the equipment for yoga. This applies to whoever, having performed a magnificent worship and having paid homage to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, should revolve this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā.

One should perform every kind of worship for all the Tathāgatas, all the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, all the Bodhisattvas, and all the mudrās, mantras, and vidyā-deities of the Tathāgatas. At midnight, having recited [the mantra] three or four times, those deities— becoming joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and mental well-being—
will cause the Blessed Lady Vasudhārā herself to come and rain down a shower of wealth, grain, and gold.

With joy in the teaching of the Tathāgata; with joy in the designation of the Buddha; with joy in the designation of the Dharma; with joy in the designation of the Saṅgha; with joy in the designation of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; with joy in the designation of the mudrās, mantras, vidyās, and deities residing in the five families; and with the intention of the Dharma-preacher.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Vasudhārā!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śrīvajradharasāgaranirghoṣa!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Oṃ, homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas. Homage to all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kṣemaṅkara; homage to the Tathāgata Vajradharasāgaragambhīra.

Homage to the Blessed Ones, the Buddhas beginning with Vipaśyin, who have attained the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, who have fulfilled the perfection of generosity, and who possess the splendor and supernatural power of Vipaśyin, as well as the wisdom of Śikhin and Viśvabhū.
By the power of Krakucchanda, by the training of Kanakamuni,
by the virtues of Kāśyapa, and by the vigor of Śākyasiṃha; by the vow of Maitreya, may these mantra-words of mine, the Tathāgata, be fulfilled.
This knowledge-mantra (*vidyā*) is for the benefit of all sentient beings; it is a liberation from the ocean of poverty, disease, suffering, and calamity.
I shall now proclaim this secret knowledge-mantra named *Vasudhārā*.
I call to mind the mantra-words whose meaning was spoken by the Tathāgata.
It is as follows: Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ oṃ śrīdhane dhane aiśvarye śukramāṇe akṣayakośe cintitotpādani manasi sādhani mano-icchā-sādhani.
O performer of accomplishments!

O you who dwell in the citadel, in the lower citadel, O sovereign of the citadels! You who cause the increase of infinite and boundless jewels, garments, ornaments, and finery; you who bring about the increase of wealth and grain; you whose arising is upon thought; you who subjugate; you who milk the treasury and granary of Śakra!
O you who steal the mantra of Bṛhaspati!

O you who are in the truth of the Buddha, the truth of the Dharma, the truth of the Saṅgha, the truth of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the truth of those intent on awakening, the truth of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, the truth of Brahmā, the truth of Viṣṇu, the truth of Rudra, and the truth of the World-Protectors; O you who carry out the commands of the Giver of Wealth!
For the abundance of all things— gold, fine gold, jewels, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, native copper, silver, emeralds, rubies, sapphires, and karketana stones—
he exercises sovereignty over sixty-four thousand varieties of grain.
Come, O Blessed One, you who possess the ocean-like depth of the Buddha’s truth, you who speak the truth!
Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu hulu hulu mulu mulu / lu lu lu lu lu / le le le le /

Iṭi 2 miṭi 2 sara 2 saṃsara 2 vigata sa ihāgacchāgaccha! O Blessed One, Vasudhārā, fulfill the desires of my mind and those of all sentient beings, and cause them to come to the houses of the practitioners.
O Blessed One, arise! All the Blessed Buddhas of the Vidyās command this: svāhā!
Homage to those of the three times!
Homage to all Tathāgatas!
It is as follows:
Oṃ, homage to the Triple Gem!
Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi!
Oṃ, homage to Vajrakrodha,
the Great Fierce One with Terrifying Protruding Fangs!
To him who holds a sword, a mace, an axe, and a noose in his hands:

Oṃ Amṛtakuṇḍali! Kha kha khāhi 2! Tiṣṭha 2! Bandha 2! Hana 2! Daha 2! Paca 2! Mara 2! Garjja 2! Visphoṭaya 2! To the one who brings an end to the life of Mahāgaṇapati and all obstructing spirits and Vināyakas: Hūṃ 2 Phaṭ Svāhā!
Oṃ sumbhani sumbhani hūṃ, gṛhṇa 2, gṛhṇāpaya 2, hūṃ, ānaya ho bhagavan vidyārāja hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hana hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ āharite mahābale hūṃ svāhā!
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ svāhā / Oṃ āḥ sitātapatre hūṃ svāhā / Oṃ maṇipadme hūṃ svāhā /
Oṃ vajradharme hūṃ svāhā / Oṃ sarvaviśuddhidharmatā vajrasiddhi hūṃ svāhā / Oṃ sarvatathāgatajñānayogīśvari hūṃ svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsarvatathāgatabhavāya svāhā / Oṃ prajñe 2 mahāprajñe śrutismṛtivijaye svāhā / Oṃ cale cule cunde svāhā /
Namely: Oṃ śrīsaubhāgyarūpe svāhā / Oṃ śrīdivyarūpe svāhā / Oṃ śrīdīptarūpe svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsurūpe svāhā / Oṃ śrīrūpamate svāhā / Oṃ śrīrūpaśobhe svāhā /
Oṃ śrīrūpamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīsuvarṇavapurūpe svāhā / Oṃ śrījñānarūpe svāhā /
Oṃ śrīprajñāpāramite svāhā / Oṃ śrīvajrasattvahṛdaye svāhā / Oṃ śrībhadre svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsubhadre svāhā / Oṃ śrīsubhadramati svāhā / Oṃ śrīmaṅgale svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsumaṅgale svāhā / Oṃ śrīmaṅgalamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīālaye svāhā /
Oṃ śrī ale ale svāhā / Oṃ śrī amale svāhā / Oṃ śrī vimale svāhā /
Oṃ śrīnirmale svāhā / Oṃ śrīmalanāśani svāhā / Oṃ śrīacale svāhā /
Oṃ śrīcale svāhā / Oṃ śrīacapale śrīacalabale svāhā /
Oṃ śrīudghāṭani svāhā / Oṃ śrīudbhedani svāhā / Oṃ śrīudbhāṣiṇi svāhā /
Oṃ śrī-udghoṣaṇi svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-prīyaṅkari svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-prītikari svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-śriyaṅkari svāhā / Oṃ śrī-śivaṅkari svāhā / Oṃ śrī-śubhaṅkari svāhā /
Oṃ śrīśrīkari svāhā / Oṃ śrīkīrtikari svāhā / Oṃ śrīlakṣmīkari svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsatyavati svāhā / Oṃ śrīśasyavati svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhanavati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīdhānyavati svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhanakari svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhānyakari svāhā /
Oṃ śrīdhane dhane svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhaneśvare svāhā / Oṃ śrīśrīmati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīprabhāmati svāhā / Oṃ śrīruru svāhā / Oṃ śrīsurūpamale svāhā /
Oṃ śrīvigatamale svāhā / Oṃ śrīvipulagarbhe svāhā / Oṃ śrīakṣayamate svāhā /
Oṃ śrī-akṣayakośe svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-dharmadade mokṣaprade svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-icchāprade svāhā!
Oṃ śrī sarvasukhaprade svāhā!
Oṃ śrī dhanade dhanapūjite svāhā!
Oṃ śrī apacāyanīye svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-ajamukhe svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-arcanyeye svāhā! Oṃ śrī-arcanāste svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-anante svāhā / Oṃ śrī-ananaste vinanaste svāhā / Oṃ śrī-vinaste svāhā /
Oṃ śrīvinanaste svāhā / Oṃ śrīviśvaste svāhā / Oṃ śrīviśvakeśi svāhā /
Oṃ śrīviśuddhaśīle svāhā / Oṃ śrīviśvarṣi svāhā / Oṃ śrīviśuddharūpe svāhā /
Oṃ śrīviguṇi viguṇiṣe viguṇe svāhā / Oṃ śrīviguṇiṣe svāhā / Oṃ śrīaṅkure svāhā /
Oṃ śrīmaṅkure svāhā / Oṃ śrīprabhaṅkure svāhā / Oṃ śrīamoghāṅkuśe jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ svāhā /
Oṃ śrī-ākarṣaṇi svāhā / Oṃ śrī-āveśani svāhā / Oṃ śrī-praveśani svāhā /
Oṃ śrīririme svāhā / Oṃ śrīrurume svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhadhame svāhā /
Oṃ śrīdhidhime svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhudhume svāhā / Oṃ śrīkhakhame svāhā /
Oṃ śrī khukhume svāhā / Oṃ śrī tara tara svāhā / Oṃ śrī tatara svāhā /

Oṃ śrī tare taratare tāra tame merura virura tāraya 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrī may the Blessed One named Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī deliver me and all sentient beings at the arrival of my wish! Oṃ śrī bhagavati oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā / Oṃ śrī bhagavati, you who are named Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī, perform great protection, defense, and concealment for me! Svāhā!
Oṃ śrīvajre vajre mahāvajre svāhā / Oṃ śrīvajropame svāhā / Oṃ śrīmahāvajropame svāhā /
Oṃ śrī-āvartani svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-pravartani svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-niṣpādani svāhā!
Oṃ śrīvasudhāre svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasuṃ dade vasudhe kuru 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrīṭakke 2 svāhā /
Oṃ śrīṭhakke 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrīḍakke 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrīḍhakke 2 svāhā /
Oṃ śrītukke 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrībhukke 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrībukke 2 svāhā /
Oṃ śrīḍhakke 2 svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhakke svāhā / Oṃ śrīvarṣaṇi svāhā /
Oṃ śrīpravarṣaṇi svāhā!
Oṃ śrīutthāpini svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the truth of the Tathāgata named Śrīvajradharasāgaranirghoṣa, thrice! Svāhā!

Oṃ, remember the truth of all the Tathāgatas, remember, remember, remember—svāhā! Oṃ, remember the truth of all the Buddhas, remember, remember, remember—svāhā! Oṃ, remember the truth of all phenomena, remember, remember, remember—svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the truth of the Śrī-saṃgha! 3 Svāhā!

Oṃ, Śrī-Taṭa, fulfill all the hopes of myself, my retinue, and all sentient beings! 2 In the home of myself and all sentient beings—whether it be in the sky, on the earth, in the water, on dry land, or in the intermediate space—[grant your presence].

Whether situated on the earth, in heaven, among mortals, in the netherworld (pātāla), in the ocean, within the seven continents, everywhere, or at the ends of the mountains— O Blessed Vasudhārā, let there be many jewels in this house, such as gems, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, silver, emeralds, musāragalva, karketana, rubies, sapphires, and so forth.
May gold, silver, copper, iron, the roots of minerals, life-sustaining substances, and so forth; may my various riches, grains, and the sixty-four thousand varieties of rice;
and may my treasuries, granaries, and all utensils for myself and all sentient beings—be nourished! Svāhā!
Oṃ, Śrī, fulfill [all needs]! Svāhā!
Oṃ śrīmaṅgale svāhā / Oṃ śrīsumaṅgale svāhā / Oṃ śrīmaṅgalamati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsumaṅgalamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīśubhamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīśāntamati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīśubhamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīmahāśubhamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīmahāmati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīmahārthamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīprabhāvamati svāhā / Oṃ śrībhadramati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīśubhabhadramati svāhā / Oṃ śrījayamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīvijayamati svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsucandramati svāhā.
Oṃ śrīgurviṇīsukhena prasūtani mahātejaḥ śrī svāhā.
Oṃ śāntamati svāhā.
Oṃ śrīmahāpauṣṭamati svāhā / Oṃ śrīsarvajanavaśaṃkari svāhā / Oṃ śrīsarvaduṣṭanikṛntani svāhā /
Oṃ śrī sarvaśatruvināśani hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ śrī āgaccha āgaccha samayam anusmara svāhā / Oṃ śrī hṛdayam anusmara svāhā /
Oṃ, Śrī, remember the *upahṛdaya*; svāhā! Oṃ, Śrī, remember the *āvaraṇa*; svāhā! Oṃ, Śrī, remember the *ādhāra*; svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the glorious power, svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the glorious intrinsic nature, svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the glorious steadfastness, svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the glorious victory, svāhā! Oṃ, remember the glorious triumph, svāhā!
Oṃ, remember the pledge of all sentient beings, svāhā!
Oṃ śrī sarvatathāgatavinayam anusmara svāhā / Oṃ śrī vasudhāre svāhā / Oṃ śrī vasudhā svāhā /
Oṃ śrīvasudhe svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasumukhi svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasudhāre svāhā /
Oṃ śrīvasudhe svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasudhari svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasumati priye svāhā /
Oṃ śrī-vasudhāraṇīye svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-vasumati śriye svāhā!
Oṃ śrī-vasudhare dharaṇī dhāraṇī vasudhāraṇīye svāhā!
Oṃ śrīlakṣmīye svāhā / Oṃ śrīlakṣmīnivāsanīye svāhā / Oṃ śrībhūtalanivāsinīye svāhā /
Oṃ śrīvasudhe svāhā / Oṃ śrīśriye śrīkari dhanakari dhānyakari vrī svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasudhāre svāhā /
Oṃ śrīsamaye saumyasamayakari mahāsamaye svāhā / Oṃ śrīdhanadhānyasamaye śrīkari vasuṃdhare vasudhe svāhā /

Oṃ śrīvasudhāre svāhā / Oṃ śrīvasudhāre, come, come, O Blessed One! Remember your pledge; grant me accomplishment, hūṃ svāhā! Oṃ śrīvasudhārā, to you, the dhāraṇī who bestows boons, with all wealth, grain, jewels, garments, ornaments, and all types of crops...

Grant me abundance with all requisites; grant it to all sentient beings as well. Bestow upon me peace, nourishment, power, and accomplishment—svāhā! Oṃ, we meditate on the one who brings glory, wealth, and grain; we meditate on all jewels, ornaments, and requisites. May the glorious Vasudhārā inspire us—svāhā! Oṃ āḥ svāhā!
Oṃ svaḥ svāhā / Oṃ hrīḥ svāhā / Oṃ svā svāhā /
Oṃ hoḥ svāhā!

Oṃ, you who carry the vessel of the vehicle, you who go far, you who bring about the production of goods not yet produced, and you who cause the increase of goods already produced; ṭili 2 ṭeli 2 iṭa 2! Come, come, O Blessed One! Do not delay for me or for all sentient beings!

And fulfill my heart's desire from the ten directions: just as streams of water completely fill the earth; just as the sun dispels darkness with its rays; just as he causes all medicinal herbs to grow by means of the moon;
and just as great medicinal herbs destroy all diseases.

May Dhanada, Varuṇa, Indra, and likewise Vaivasvata, as well as the great Manonugāminī, constantly contemplate success; may they all immediately bestow [it] according to desire, so that the mantra-words here may be accomplished. Namely: Oṃ kheṭe 2 khiṭi 2 khuṭu 2 chucu 2 muru 2 muruṇḍa (Vdh-DH_140).
2. Oṃ tarpaya dehi dadāpaya svāhā! Oṃ uttiṣṭha hiraṇyasuvarṇadhāre svāhā!
Oṃ vastrābharaṇāya svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to food and drink! Oṃ, svāhā to the treasury of wealth! Oṃ, svāhā to the shower of wealth!
Oṃ, to the Lord of the Earth, svāhā!
Oṃ, to Vasudhā, svā svāhā! Oṃ, to Gau, svāhā!

"Bestow security, health, and wealth; cause [them] to be given, svāhā!
This is the heart-mantra of the Blessed Lady. Even for one who has committed great sinful deeds, these mantra-words bring success;
how much more so for a person endowed with faith and resolve? It bestows great wealth equal to a man's stature.
It fulfills one's desired wishes:
Oṃ vajre vajre mahāvajre vajropame ṭake ṭhake hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ śriye śrīkari dhanakari dhānyakari ehi āgacchāgaccha vrīṃ svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to the Śaṅkha treasure-vessel! Oṃ, svāhā to the Padma treasure-vessel! Oṃ, [homage] to the eight yakṣiṇīs! (Vdh-DH_143)
Sarvapūjā hūṃ svāhā! Oṃ! Whatever desires one may desire here, all those desired things he shall fulfill completely.
May the mantra words be efficacious!

Namely: *Namaḥ ratnatrayāya*. Oṃ, homage to the Goddess, daughter of the Giver of Wealth; cause Vasudhārā to rain down, rain down! O Mistress of Wealth, whose body is jewels, *huru* 2! O Mistress of Wealth!

Give me jewels! Cause [jewels] to be given! O Great Treasure of the Jewel-Ocean, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of millions of treasures, come, come, Blessed One Vasudhārā! Having entered my city, my abode, cause a great treasure to fall! 2 tura 2 kuru 2 hūṃ phaṭ! O dweller on Kailāśa, svāhā!
Householder, this is that dhāraṇī-mantra called Vasudhārā.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, diseases, famine, pestilence, and the like have no power.
Furthermore, noble son, whoever, having performed worship to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, should recite these mantra-words of the Vasudhārā dhāraṇī for six months;
Then one becomes accomplished.
In whichever direction this vidyā is maintained, that direction becomes honored.
In whatever place it is worshipped—for the sake of nourishment—whether in one’s own house or another’s house—with faith and supreme faith.
Having spread out an image of the Noble Lady Vasudhārā, or a painted cloth [depicting her], before him, one should prepare a square mandala with sandalwood.

Then, having performed worship according to one's means— adorned with flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and provided with offerings of food and various services— one should also have the Dharma-preacher bathe in fragrant water.
Having dressed in clean garments with fragrant limbs and sat upon a peacock seat, or having placed an image, a cloth painting, or the like before him,

and recollecting that very [deity], one should worship at the time of sunrise; then, from the daily undertaking of the vow without interruption, one should recite the dhāraṇī continuously throughout the entire night.

In due course, all prosperity shall accrue to him. Therefore, having spent the night according to the aforementioned rule, he should again, at dawn, bathe in fragrant water, clothe himself in clean and spotless garments, and, becoming a celibate practitioner, recite this dhāraṇī together with its introduction continuously in a pure place.
Three times over, then,
whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family, they fill their home with a great measure of wealth and grain;
and by means of all riches, grain, silver, gold, and all necessary utensils, they cause all calamities to perish.

Alternatively, at dawn, having bathed in fragrant water, dressed in pure and stainless garments, abstaining from intoxicants, eating food that is meatless, saltless, and non-fleshy, and observing celibacy, one should— either in one’s own house, another’s house, or in an auspicious place such as a treasury or granary— for the sake of prosperity, prepare a square mandala with sandalwood paste for the Blessed One, the glorious Āryāvalokiteśvara.

Having performed an extensive worship according to one's means before the Tathāgata, all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the deity of the mahāmudrā-mantra-vidyā, one should— being well-composed, with a single thought-moment, and with an intention for the welfare and happiness of the donor— contemplate that very Blessed Lady with faith and supreme faith, reciting this dhāraṇī together with its causal basis.
One should recite it continuously for one day and night, or for seven days and nights, without interruption.
The preceptor, likewise according to the rule, should worship with all the offerings of bali three times during the night and three times during the day.
In the same manner, the patron of the gift should also perform everything according to the rule.
During the times of recitation, one should give gifts of gold and other valuables according to one's ability;
thereby, the practice becomes perfected through recitation.
Then, in a mere instant, O Householder, the Vasudhārā that is the measure of a Great Being completely fills the house of the donor with a flow of wealth.
"It destroys all loss of wealth, grain, silver, gold, and all utensils, as well as all calamities.
Therefore, householder, with every effort, take up this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā; maintain it, recite it, teach it, cause others to grasp it, master it, and reveal it extensively to others," he said.
"Then it will lead to long-lasting benefit, welfare, happiness, enjoyment, the equipment for yoga, security, and abundance.
"Therefore, it is well, Blessed One," [he replied].

Having heard the words of the Blessed One, the householder named Sucandra, having heard this dhāraṇī called Vasudhārā from the presence of the Blessed One, was thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheer. Prostrating at the feet of the Blessed One and joining his palms in reverence, he addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, I have grasped this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā; it has been humbly received, maintained, recited, mastered, rejoiced in, well-pondered by the mind, and explained in detail to others. Now, I shall proclaim it.
Then, at that very moment, the householder named Sucandra found his treasuries and granaries completely full.

Then the householder Sucandra, having circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and looking back at the Blessed One again and again, departed from the presence of the Blessed One for his own home.
Having departed and entered within, that householder beheld [his home] fully enriched with all kinds of wealth, grain, and jewels.

Seeing that the treasuries and granaries were filled with all kinds of requisites, he was struck with wonder; joyful, satisfied, elated, uplifted in mind, and filled with gladness, joy, and cheerfulness, his heart became soft and tender through the roots of merit as he delighted in the Buddha, the Blessed One, whose every aspiration was fulfilled.
With intense love, profound respect, and reverent devotion toward the *Vasudhārā* dhāraṇī, he felt inspired by its grace.
And Citrikāra generated the thought of awakening.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:

"Go, Ānanda, and look at the house of the householder Sucandra, which is filled with an abundance of all kinds of wealth and grain, and whose great treasuries and storehouses are full of all manner of jewels, gold, and utensils."
And they were all complete.
Then the venerable Ānanda, having heard the words of the Blessed One, went toward the great city of Kośāmbī, to the residence of Sucandra; having approached that house and entered inside, he saw it.

Seeing that all wealth and grain were abundant and fully supplied, and that the great treasuries and storehouses were completely filled, the venerable Ānanda was thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he approached the Blessed One, and having approached, being struck with wonder and filled with gladness and happiness, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and addressed him thus:

“Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder named Sucandra was born so wealthy, possessing great enjoyments, and enriched with vast treasuries, granaries, wealth, grain, bullion, gold, and various kinds of jewels? The Blessed One said, “Faithful Ānanda, the householder named Sucandra was supremely faithful, possessed of a noble intention, and steadfast.”
And by him this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā was recited, set in motion, mastered, maintained, read, fully understood, rejoiced in, and extensively proclaimed to others.
Therefore, Ānanda, he said: "You too should master this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā; maintain it, recite it, and teach it."

Cause it to be grasped, master it, and reveal it extensively to others; it will be for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings— both gods and humans— for that householder, Ānanda, in whose hands this dhāraṇī shall come to reside, whether held in hand or kept in a book.
It will be held in the heart, maintained, recited, contemplated, entered into the hearing, brought into the home, placed in a book, and honored.
For such a person, there will be no fear of famine;
gradually, their prosperity will increase.

“Ānanda, for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings— both gods and humans— I do not perceive any such phenomenon in this world with its gods,
Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods, humans, and asuras, who could alter or transgress this knowledge by means of speech;
such a possibility does not exist.”

For what reason? Because, Ānanda, these mantra-words of the *dhāraṇī* named Vasudhārā are indeed indestructible; they will not even come to the path of hearing for those whose roots of merit are exhausted.
How much less so for those who shall hold them in books or in their hearts, and recite them!
For what reason? Because this *dhāraṇī* has been spoken by all the Tathāgatas, empowered, and sealed with their own seal.
It has been revealed, rejoiced in, brought forth, praised, extolled, disclosed, made clear, announced, declared,
for the sake, welfare, happiness, enjoyment, utilization, and security of poor beings who are oppressed by various diseases and afflicted by the fear and calamities of all wicked beings.
Ānanda said: "Blessed One, I have grasped this *dhāraṇī* named Vasudhārā; it has been retained, recited, mastered, rejoiced in, and well-pondered by my mind. Excellent, Blessed One!

Then the venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, he addressed the Blessed One.
Having looked at her face, he then spoke these verses at that time:
"May there always be inconceivable abundance of wealth, with many jewels and well-provided gold;
may this house be filled with a mandala—homage to you, Śrī Vasudhārā, forever!"
The Blessed Buddha reflected that the Buddha-dharma is also inconceivable;
he reflected that for those who have gained faith, the maturation [of that faith] is likewise inconceivable.
O Teacher, Knower of All, lineage of the Dharma Kings,
you who have attained the fruit of reaching the further shore— homage be to you, the Heroic Buddha!

Then, indeed, the venerable Ānanda, having heard this Dharma-discourse from the presence of the Blessed One, thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness, said this to the Blessed One:
"What is the name of this Dharma-discourse, O Blessed One? How, O Blessed One, should I remember this Dharma-discourse?"

The Blessed One said: "Ānanda, remember this as 'The Inquiry of the Householder Sucandra'; remember it also as 'The Treasury of All Wealth, Grain, Silver, Gold, and Jewels'; remember it also as 'Praised by All Tathāgatas'; and remember it also as 'The Ritual for the Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī Empowered by All Tathāgatas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the Venerable Ānanda, those monks, and those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were uplifted in mind."
And that entire assembly—the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
Thus ends the noble sūtra of the dhāraṇī named Śrī Vasudhārā.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
